core.title: Build every new component URN with the stack's single canonical URN builder
core.given: A component URN is created, changed, or reused
core.then: Build every new or changed component URN through the stack's single canonical component-URN builder (the utility named by the profile) — never hand-typed or string-concatenated — and reuse only component URNs that were produced by that builder.
avoid: Hand-typing or string-concatenating a new component URN.
core.why: A single builder gives the graph one stable URN form.
evidence: For each new or changed component URN there is an actual invocation of the canonical builder (in code, or recorded with its arguments in a plan artifact or tooling output) whose arguments are the URN's declared segments.
Each reused component URN traces to a URN that was produced by that builder.
verification: The check looks for the builder invocation itself (in code, or recorded with its arguments in a plan artifact or tooling output); a URN that merely matches the component URN shape does not pass — output equality alone does not prove builder use.
Reuse is no loophole: a referenced or copied component URN that was never produced by the canonical builder fails this rule.
The builder's identity, call signature and argument order are realization details supplied by the profile; the core names only 'the single canonical component-URN builder'.
Scope: the rule fires wherever a component URN is created, changed or reused, in any artifact, with no exemption for hand-authored declarations; a changed URN counts as a new one.

Recognition never requires shape conformance first: a component URN that is declared or otherwise recognizable counts even when malformed (for example missing or extra segments). The profile's component URN shape is used only to identify the component URN kind and to interpret a URN's segments — never to exempt a nonmatching declaration from the invocation or reuse-traceability obligations.

values: new or changed component URN in any artifact
canonical component-URN builder call added or edited

fires: A new component URN is created in any artifact (plan artifacts, manifests, acceptance and test definitions, docs, source code, tooling), including hand-authored declarations and declarations that do not match the profile's component URN shape.
An existing component URN is changed in any segment, which counts as creating a new URN.
A component URN is referenced or copied: it must be one that was built by the canonical builder.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's single canonical utility that constructs a component URN; every new or changed component URN must be produced by an invocation of it, and every reused component URN must trace to its output.

The component URN shape, used to identify the component URN kind and to interpret a component URN's segments (and thus the builder's arguments). It is not a prerequisite for this rule's scope: a declared or recognizable component URN that does not match the shape remains subject to the builder-use and reuse-traceability obligations.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's single canonical utility that constructs a component URN, with its call signature; convention cores that require builder-mediated URN construction refer to it instead of naming a utility.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group defines URN shapes and binding/declaration syntax (urn.<artifact>, urn.binding.<artifact>, urn.declaration) but no key names the construct that BUILDS a URN; tooling.urn_resolver only resolves an existing URN to its artifact. The key generalizes parametrically to urn.builder.<artifact> for other artifact kinds.

bunOnly.text: Utility: utils.graph.URNBuilder.component(wagon_id, feature_id, component_name, side, layer). Its argument order matches the URN segment order.
bunOnly.reason: Names the Bun utility's module path, call signature, and an argument-order property specific to that utility; the core takes the builder's identity and signature from the profile and states only generically (in verification) that they are realization details.
A task term naming the Bun utility; the neutral core keeps only stack-neutral task terms, and the utility's name is profile data, not core vocabulary.
The change value names the Bun utility; the neutral core says 'canonical component-URN builder call added or edited'.

Neutralized change values; the original second value names the Bun utility, kept as bunOnly. The diff observer for new or changed component URNs does not gate on the profile's component URN shape; shape interpretation is kept out of recognition (see verification).

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral: every new or changed component URN must be produced by the stack's single canonical builder, and reused URNs must trace to that builder; the core keeps the no-hand-concatenation rule, the reuse clause, the 'changed URN counts as new' clause and the no-exemption-for-hand-authored-declarations scope, and adds nothing. Recognition of a component URN never requires conformance to the profile's component URN shape: declared or recognizable component URNs stay in scope even when malformed, and the shape is used only to interpret segments, matching the Bun observer note that identifies component URNs by their 'component:' strings. Everything concrete is delegated: the utility's module path, signature, argument names and the argument-order observation (verifier_detail[0]) and the 'URNBuilder.component' task term are Bun-only; the builder's identity enters the core only through the proposed key urn.builder.component. urn.component is listed because the core must interpret component URN segments and read builder arguments; bun.json itself refers to URNs only by their 'component:' prefix (activation note), so the bunValue shown is the component URN shape carried by the sibling split rule planner.component.urn and the profile. bun.json declares no prefer or unless items and no severity or disposition, so the core adds none.
